newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, gilt volume slips.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, gilt volume slips.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 0.25-0.50 percent range at the close on Thursday, little down from the day's opening quotes of 0.50-1.00 percent, dealers said.
"The market was dull, all the players had covered positions in view of reporting Friday," a dealer said.

He said call opened at one percent and slipped to 0.50 percent with lenders quiet. "The next fortnight may see call rates rallying to six percent on Saturday and will move in a downward direction from Monday," he said.
Dealers said securities prices were in tandem with the previous close, despite low call rates.
"Good liquidity, less rise in credit and prevailing uncertainty on the political front affected market sentiment," a dealer at state-run bank said.
There was interest in securities maturing in year 2000 to 2002, dealers said.

The price rose by three basis points on 13.55 percent 2001 stock and 12.50 percent 2004 stock by 100.33 rupees and 94.78 rupees, respectively against Wednesday's close, while 13.50 percent 1997 stock was unchanged at 100.86 rupees, they said.
"Volumes on the National Stock Exchange slipped to 1.23 billion rupees on Thursday, compared to 2.78 billion rupees earlier," said Chandra Shetty at Mata Securities India.
The latest auctioned 364 day treasury bill was traded in the region of 10.20-10.30 percent yield to maturity compared to its auctioned yield of 10.35 percent, dealers said.

The treasury bill maturing in August 1997 was traded at a yield of 9.30 percent, compared to its previous 9.25 percent, while the treasury bill maturing in January 1997 was traded at a yield of 6.85 percent, against the Wednesday's of 7.10 percent, dealers said.
